claim: Clustered protocadherins (cPcdhs) are a large family of cadherin-like proteins named for the clustered arrangement of their genes in vertebrate genomes.
source: Clustered protocadherins (cPcdhs) are a large family of cadherin-like proteins named for the clustered arrangement of their genes in vertebrate genomes (Wu and Maniatis, 1999; Wu et al., 2001).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature (Wu and Maniatis, 1999; Wu et al., 2001).

claim: cPcdhs play roles in many facets of neural development.
source: cPcdhs play roles in many facets of neural development (Peek et al., 2017), including circuit development, most notably neurite self-avoidance in vertebrates (Kostadinov and Sanes, 2015; Lefebvre et al., 2012; Mountoufaris et al., 2017), and tiling (Chen et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature (Peek et al., 2017; Kostadinov and Sanes, 2015; Lefebvre et al., 2012; Mountoufaris et al., 2017; Chen et al., 2017).

claim: In self-avoidance, neurites from the same neuron (sister neurites) actively avoid one another, whereas neurons from different neurons can freely interact.
source: In self-avoidance, neurites from the same neuron (sister neurites) actively avoid one another, whereas neurons from different neurons can freely interact.
evidence: The claim draws from established scientific understanding of self-avoidance mechanisms.

claim: Tiling is similar to self-avoidance, but in tiling all neurons acquire the same identity, so that there is uniform repulsion among self- and nonself-neurites.
source: Tiling is similar to self-avoidance, but in tiling all neurons acquire the same identity, so that there is uniform repulsion among self- and nonself-neurites (Chen et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior literature (Chen et al., 2017).

claim: Self-avoidance among sister neurites leads to the characteristic arbor structures of dendritic trees, and prevents the formation of self-synapses.
source: Self-avoidance among sister neurites leads to the characteristic arbor structures of dendritic trees, and prevents the formation of self-synapses (Kostadinov and Sanes, 2015; Lefebvre et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature (Kostadinov and Sanes, 2015; Lefebvre et al., 2012).

claim: For arthropod invertebrates such as Drosophila melanogaster, self-avoidance is mediated by immunoglobulin superfamily Dscam1 cell surface proteins.
source: For arthropod invertebrates such as Drosophila melanogaster, self-avoidance is mediated by immunoglobulin superfamily Dscam1 cell surface proteins.
evidence: The claim draws from established scientific knowledge about Drosophila self-avoidance mechanisms.

claim: The stochastic alternative splicing of Dscam1 pre-mRNAs can, in principle, generate 19,008 distinct extracellular isoforms.
source: The stochastic alternative splicing of Dscam1 pre-mRNAs can, in principle, generate 19,008 distinct extracellular isoforms; the vast majority of which, based on ELISA-based binding assays, mediate homophilic recognition (Miura et al., 2013; Schmucker et al., 2000; Wojtowicz et al., 2004; Wojtowicz et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature (Miura et al., 2013; Schmucker et al., 2000; Wojtowicz et al., 2004; Wojtowicz et al., 2007).

claim: The vast majority of Dscam1 isoforms mediate homophilic recognition based on ELISA-based binding assays.
source: The stochastic alternative splicing of Dscam1 pre-mRNAs can, in principle, generate 19,008 distinct extracellular isoforms; the vast majority of which, based on ELISA-based binding assays, mediate homophilic recognition (Miura et al., 2013; Schmucker et al., 2000; Wojtowicz et al., 2004; Wojtowicz et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature describing ELISA-based binding assays (Miura et al., 2013; Schmucker et al., 2000; Wojtowicz et al., 2004; Wojtowicz et al., 2007).

claim: Each Drosophila neuron expresses a repertoire estimated at 10–50 Dscam1 isoforms.
source: Each Drosophila neuron expresses a repertoire estimated at 10–50 isoforms and the large number of Dscam1 isoforms ensures a low probability that any two contacting neurons will have an identical or even a similar isoform repertoire thus minimizing the chance of inappropriate avoidance between nonself-neurons (Hattori et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior literature (Hattori et al., 2009).

claim: The large number of Dscam1 isoforms ensures a low probability that any two contacting neurons will have an identical or even a similar isoform repertoire thus minimizing the chance of inappropriate avoidance between nonself-neurons.
source: Each Drosophila neuron expresses a repertoire estimated at 10–50 isoforms and the large number of Dscam1 isoforms ensures a low probability that any two contacting neurons will have an identical or even a similar isoform repertoire thus minimizing the chance of inappropriate avoidance between nonself-neurons (Hattori et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior literature (Hattori et al., 2009).

claim: In mammalian nervous systems, cPcdh isoform expression is controlled by the unique organization of three tandem gene clusters, Pcdhα, Pcdhβ, and Pcdhγ.
source: In mammalian nervous systems, cPcdh isoform expression is controlled by the unique organization of three tandem gene clusters, Pcdhα, Pcdhβ, and Pcdhγ (Wu and Maniatis, 1999), with each cluster containing multiple variable exons, which encode full cPcdh ectodomain regions with six extracellular cadherin (EC) domains, a single transmembrane region, and a short cytoplasmic extension (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior literature (Wu and Maniatis, 1999) and reference to Figure 1A.

claim: Each cPcdh gene cluster contains multiple variable exons, which encode full cPcdh ectodomain regions with six extracellular cadherin (EC) domains, a single transmembrane region, and a short cytoplasmic extension.
source: In mammalian nervous systems, cPcdh isoform expression is controlled by the unique organization of three tandem gene clusters, Pcdhα, Pcdhβ, and Pcdhγ (Wu and Maniatis, 1999), with each cluster containing multiple variable exons, which encode full cPcdh ectodomain regions with six extracellular cadherin (EC) domains, a single transmembrane region, and a short cytoplasmic extension (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior literature (Wu and Maniatis, 1999) and reference to Figure 1A.

claim: The Pcdhα and Pcdhγ gene clusters contain three 'constant' exons that encode cluster-specific intracellular domains.
source: The Pcdhα and Pcdhγ gene clusters also contain three 'constant' exons that encode cluster-specific intracellular domains.
evidence: The claim draws from established knowledge about cPcdh gene structure.

claim: The last two variable exons in the Pcdhα gene cluster and the last three variable exons of the Pcdhγ gene cluster diverge in sequence from other cPcdh isoforms and are referred to as 'C-type' cPcdhs.
source: The last two variable exons in the Pcdhα gene cluster and the last three variable exons of the Pcdhγ gene cluster diverge in sequence from other cPcdh isoforms and are referred to as 'C-type' cPcdhs (Wu and Maniatis, 1999; Wu et al., 2001).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature (Wu and Maniatis, 1999; Wu et al., 2001).

claim: Sequence differences further subdivide Pcdhγ genes into two subfamilies – PcdhγA and PcdhγB.
source: Sequence differences further subdivide Pcdhγ genes into two subfamilies – PcdhγA and PcdhγB (Wu and Maniatis, 1999).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior literature (Wu and Maniatis, 1999).

claim: The full mouse cPcdh complement is comprised of 53 non-C-type cPcdhs (α1–12, β1–22, γA1–12, and γB1–7) and 5 C-type cPcdhs (αC1, αC2, γC3, γC4, and γC5).
source: The full mouse cPcdh complement is comprised of 53 non-C-type cPcdhs, commonly known as alternate cPcdhs (α1–12, β1–22, γA1–12, and γB1–7), whose expression choices vary stochastically between cells through alternate promoter choice (Canzio and Maniatis, 2019) and 5 C-type cPcdhs (αC1, αC2, γC3, γC4, and γC5), which are constitutively expressed.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior literature (Canzio and Maniatis, 2019).

claim: Alternate cPcdh expression choices vary stochastically between cells through alternate promoter choice.
source: The full mouse cPcdh complement is comprised of 53 non-C-type cPcdhs, commonly known as alternate cPcdhs (α1–12, β1–22, γA1–12, and γB1–7), whose expression choices vary stochastically between cells through alternate promoter choice (Canzio and Maniatis, 2019) and 5 C-type cPcdhs (αC1, αC2, γC3, γC4, and γC5), which are constitutively expressed.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior literature (Canzio and Maniatis, 2019).

claim: C-type cPcdhs are constitutively expressed.
source: The full mouse cPcdh complement is comprised of 53 non-C-type cPcdhs, commonly known as alternate cPcdhs (α1–12, β1–22, γA1–12, and γB1–7), whose expression choices vary stochastically between cells through alternate promoter choice (Canzio and Maniatis, 2019) and 5 C-type cPcdhs (αC1, αC2, γC3, γC4, and γC5), which are constitutively expressed.
evidence: The claim draws from established knowledge about C-type cPcdh expression patterns.

claim: Olfactory sensory neurons express ~5–10 cPcdhs stochastically.
source: cPcdh expression, either stochastic or constitutive, varies between cell types: for example, olfactory sensory neurons express ~5–10 cPcdhs stochastically; Purkinje neurons express ~10 alternate cPcdhs stochastically and all five C-types constitutively (Esumi et al., 2005; Kaneko et al., 2006); and serotonergic neurons express just αC2 constitutively (Canzio and Maniatis, 2019; Chen et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature (Esumi et al., 2005; Kaneko et al., 2006).

claim: Purkinje neurons express ~10 alternate cPcdhs stochastically and all five C-types constitutively.
source: cPcdh expression, either stochastic or constitutive, varies between cell types: for example, olfactory sensory neurons express ~5–10 cPcdhs stochastically; Purkinje neurons express ~10 alternate cPcdhs stochastically and all five C-types constitutively (Esumi et al., 2005; Kaneko et al., 2006); and serotonergic neurons express just αC2 constitutively (Canzio and Maniatis, 2019; Chen et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature (Esumi et al., 2005; Kaneko et al., 2006).

claim: Serotonergic neurons express just αC2 constitutively.
source: cPcdh expression, either stochastic or constitutive, varies between cell types: for example, olfactory sensory neurons express ~5–10 cPcdhs stochastically; Purkinje neurons express ~10 alternate cPcdhs stochastically and all five C-types constitutively (Esumi et al., 2005; Kaneko et al., 2006); and serotonergic neurons express just αC2 constitutively (Canzio and Maniatis, 2019; Chen et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature (Canzio and Maniatis, 2019; Chen et al., 2017).

claim: The relatively small number of cPcdh isoforms – fewer than 60 – has presented a significant challenge to generation of sufficient diversity to provide mammalian neurons with functionally unique identities.
source: While the cPcdh and Dscam1 systems bear striking similarities, the relatively small number of cPcdh isoforms – fewer than 60 – has presented a significant challenge to generation of sufficient diversity to provide mammalian neurons with functionally unique identities.
evidence: The claim is based on logical inference from the comparison between cPcdh and Dscam1 systems.

claim: Solution biophysics and functional mutagenesis studies have shown that cPcdhs interact in trans through antiparallel interactions between their EC1–4 regions.
source: Solution biophysics and functional mutagenesis studies have shown that cPcdhs interact in trans through antiparallel interactions between their EC1–4 regions (Rubinstein et al., 2015), and crystal structures of alternate α, β, and γ cPcdh trans homodimers have revealed interfaces involving EC1 interacting with EC4 and EC2 with EC3 (Figure 1B; Goodman et al., 2016c; Goodman et al., 2016a; Nicoludis et al., 2016; Rubinstein et al., 2015; Thu et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature (Rubinstein et al., 2015) and reference to Figure 1B.

claim: Crystal structures of alternate α, β, and γ cPcdh trans homodimers have revealed interfaces involving EC1 interacting with EC4 and EC2 with EC3.
source: Solution biophysics and functional mutagenesis studies have shown that cPcdhs interact in trans through antiparallel interactions between their EC1–4 regions (Rubinstein et al., 2015), and crystal structures of alternate α, β, and γ cPcdh trans homodimers have revealed interfaces involving EC1 interacting with EC4 and EC2 with EC3 (Figure 1B; Goodman et al., 2016c; Goodman et al., 2016a; Nicoludis et al., 2016; Rubinstein et al., 2015; Thu et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature (Goodman et al., 2016c; Goodman et al., 2016a; Nicoludis et al., 2016; Rubinstein et al., 2015; Thu et al., 2014) and reference to Figure 1B.

claim: cPcdhs form cis dimers through their membrane-proximal EC5–6 regions.
source: cPcdhs also form cis dimers through their membrane-proximal EC5–6 regions, and are presented on cell surfaces as cis dimers (Goodman et al., 2017; Rubinstein et al., 2015; Thu et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature (Goodman et al., 2017; Rubinstein et al., 2015; Thu et al., 2014).

claim: cPcdhs are presented on cell surfaces as cis dimers.
source: cPcdhs also form cis dimers through their membrane-proximal EC5–6 regions, and are presented on cell surfaces as cis dimers (Goodman et al., 2017; Rubinstein et al., 2015; Thu et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature (Goodman et al., 2017; Rubinstein et al., 2015; Thu et al., 2014).

claim: Crystal structures of cis-interacting protocadherin ectodomains have revealed an asymmetrical interaction mode, where one molecule interacts through elements of EC5 and EC6, and the other interacts exclusively through EC6.
source: Crystal structures of cis-interacting protocadherin ectodomains (Brasch et al., 2019; Goodman et al., 2017) have revealed an asymmetrical interaction mode, where one molecule interacts through elements of EC5 and EC6, and the other interacts exclusively through EC6 (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature (Brasch et al., 2019; Goodman et al., 2017) and reference to Figure 1C.

claim: Rubinstein et al., 2015 proposed that cPcdhs located on apposed membrane surfaces would form an extended zipper-like lattice through alternating cis and trans interactions.
source: In order to explain how about 60 cPcdh isoforms can provide a comparable or even greater level of neuronal diversity as 19,000 Dscam isoforms, Rubinstein et al., 2015 proposed that cPcdhs located on apposed membrane surfaces would form an extended zipper-like lattice through alternating cis and trans interactions (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior literature (Rubinstein et al., 2015) and reference to Figure 1D.

claim: In self-interactions between two membranes with identical cPcdh repertoires, cPcdh chains would grow to form large structures, limited mainly by the number of molecules.
source: In self-interactions – between two membranes with identical cPcdh repertoires – these chains would grow to form large structures, limited mainly by the number of molecules (Brasch et al., 2019; Rubinstein et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature (Brasch et al., 2019; Rubinstein et al., 2015).

claim: In nonself-interactions between two membranes with differing cPcdh repertoires, large linear assemblies would not form since even a single mismatch between expressed isoforms would terminate chain assembly.
source: However, in nonself-interactions – between two membranes with differing cPcdh repertoires – such large linear assemblies would not form since even a single mismatch between expressed isoforms would terminate chain assembly (Brasch et al., 2019; Rubinstein et al., 2017; Rubinstein et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature (Brasch et al., 2019; Rubinstein et al., 2017; Rubinstein et al., 2015).

claim: The 'isoform-mismatch chain-termination model' envisions the assembly of long cPcdh chains between sites of neurite–neurite contact to represent the signature of 'self', which is then translated by downstream signaling that leads to self-avoidance.
source: This 'isoform-mismatch chain-termination model' for the 'barcoding' of vertebrate neurons envisions the assembly of long cPcdh chains between sites of neurite–neurite contact to represent the signature of 'self', which is then translated by downstream signaling that leads to self-avoidance (Fan et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior literature (Fan et al., 2018).

claim: X-ray crystallographic studies and cryo-electron tomography studies of the full-length cPcdh ectodomains bound between the surfaces of adherent liposomes revealed the existence of linear zippers.
source: X-ray crystallographic studies and cryo-electron tomography studies of the full-length cPcdh ectodomains bound between the surfaces of adherent liposomes revealed the existence of linear zippers thus providing strong evidence supporting the validity of the model (Brasch et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior literature (Brasch et al., 2019).

claim: cPcdh trans homophilic interactions are remarkably precise, with no evidence for heterophilic interactions between different cPcdh isoforms.
source: Overall, in accordance with the requirements of the isoform-mismatch chain-termination model, we find that trans homophilic interactions are remarkably precise, with no evidence for heterophilic interactions between different cPcdh isoforms.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript (SPR experiments in Figure 2).

claim: cPcdh cis interactions are largely promiscuous but with relatively weak intrasubfamily and, especially, homophilic interactions.
source: In contrast cPcdh cis interactions are largely promiscuous but with relatively weak intrasubfamily and, especially, homophilic interactions.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript (SPR and AUC experiments in Figure 4).

claim: Biotinylated ectodomain fragments containing the trans-interacting EC1–4 regions of six representative α, β, γA, and γB mouse cPcdh isoforms were generated.
source: We generated biotinylated ectodomain fragments containing the trans-interacting EC1–4 regions (Nicoludis et al., 2015; Rubinstein et al., 2015) of six representative α, β, γA, and γB mouse cPcdh isoforms – α7, β6, β8, γA8, γA9, and γB2 – which include the most closely related isoforms by sequence identity from the β and γA subfamilies (β6/8 and γA8/9) (Rubinstein et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim describes experimental methods performed in this study, supported by citations to prior literature (Nicoludis et al., 2015; Rubinstein et al., 2015).

claim: All ectodomain fragments used in SPR experiments were confirmed to form homodimers in solution by sedimentation equilibrium analytical ultracentrifugation (AUC).
source: All ectodomain fragments used in these SPR experiments were confirmed to form homodimers in solution by sedimentation equilibrium analytical ultracentrifugation (AUC) (Figure 2—source data 1), validating that these proteins are well behaved and active.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 2—source data 1.

claim: No heterophilic binding was observed for any of the analytes over any of the six surfaces in SPR experiments.
source: Remarkably, no heterophilic binding was observed for any of the analytes over any of the six surfaces (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: β6/8 and γA8/9 have 92% and 82% sequence identities, respectively, in their trans-binding EC1–4 regions.
source: Even β6/8 and γA8/9 that have 92% and 82% sequence identities, respectively, in their trans-binding EC1–4 regions exhibit no heterophilic binding.
evidence: The claim is based on sequence analysis data.

claim: β6/8 and γA8/9 exhibit no heterophilic binding despite high sequence identity.
source: Even β6/8 and γA8/9 that have 92% and 82% sequence identities, respectively, in their trans-binding EC1–4 regions exhibit no heterophilic binding.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from SPR experiments.

claim: For heterophilic trans dimers, the lower limit for the dissociation constant (KD) would be ~200 μM.
source: We estimate that, for heterophilic trans dimers, the lower limit for the dissociation constant (KD) would be ~200 μM.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from experimental data and detection limits.

claim: Mutations designed to disrupt α7, β6, and γA8 trans interaction inhibited homophilic binding.
source: Mutations designed to disrupt α7, β6, and γA8 trans interaction inhibited homophilic binding, demonstrating that the observed binding occurs via the trans interface (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A; Goodman et al., 2016a; Goodman et al., 2016c; Rubinstein et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and citations to prior literature (Goodman et al., 2016a; Goodman et al., 2016c; Rubinstein et al., 2015).

claim: Trans-interacting fragments of all four C-type cPcdhs tested showed no binding over the alternate cPcdh SPR surfaces.
source: Of note, trans-interacting fragments of all four C-type cPcdhs tested showed no binding over the alternate cPcdh SPR surfaces (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Each of the four C-type fragments binds only to its cognate partner and no other isoform.
source: Only homophilic binding was observed, with each of the four C-type fragments binding to its cognate partner and no other isoform (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Disrupting the γC5 trans interaction with the S116R mutation inhibited binding to the γC5 surface.
source: Disrupting the γC5 trans interaction with the S116R mutation (Rubinstein et al., 2015), inhibited binding to the γC5 surface, demonstrating that the observed binding occurs via the trans interface (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B and a citation to prior literature (Rubinstein et al., 2015).

claim: αC1 does not mediate cell–cell interactions in cell aggregation assays even when coexpressed with cPcdhs that facilitate cell-surface delivery of γC4.
source: In contrast to the other C-type isoforms, αC1 does not mediate cell–cell interactions in cell aggregation assays even when coexpressed with cPcdhs that facilitate cell-surface delivery of γC4 (Thu et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior literature (Thu et al., 2014).

claim: The recombinant αC1 EC1–4 fragment forms disulfide-linked multimers which are likely nonnative.
source: Although we have been able to produce an αC1 EC1–4 fragment the recombinant molecule forms disulfide-linked multimers which are likely nonnative, precluding confident examination of αC1's potential trans interactions.
evidence: The claim is based on experimental observations from protein production.

claim: The sequence of mouse αC1 reveals the EC3:EC4 linker does not contain the full complement of calcium-coordinating residues.
source: Notably, the sequence of mouse αC1 reveals the EC3:EC4 linker does not contain the full complement of calcium-coordinating residues, which may impact the structure and binding properties of this protein (Thu et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is based on sequence analysis and supported by a citation to prior literature (Thu et al., 2014).

claim: AUC was used to measure the trans homodimer KDs revealing a >200-fold range of binding affinities, from 2.9 μM (α71–5) to >500 μM (γC41–4).
source: We therefore used AUC to measure the trans homodimer KDs (Figure 2—source data 1) revealing a >200-fold range of binding affinities, from 2.9 μM (α71–5) to >500 μM (γC41–4).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 2—source data 1.

claim: All cPcdhs (except αC1) have been shown to effectively mediate cell–cell interactions in cell aggregation assays.
source: Regardless of their trans-binding affinity, all cPcdhs (except αC1) have previously been shown to effectively mediate cell–cell interactions in cell aggregation assays (Schreiner and Weiner, 2010; Thu et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature (Schreiner and Weiner, 2010; Thu et al., 2014).

claim: AUC data have confirmed that C-type cPcdhs αC2, γC3, and γC5 form trans dimers using their EC1–4 domains.
source: Despite their more divergent sequences compared with alternate cPcdhs, AUC data have confirmed that C-type cPcdhs αC2, γC3, and γC5 form trans dimers using their EC1–4 domains (Goodman et al., 2016a; Rubinstein et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature (Goodman et al., 2016a; Rubinstein et al., 2015).

claim: γC41–4 behaved as a very weak dimer in AUC (KD >500 μM).
source: However, γC41–4 behaved as a very weak dimer in AUC (KD >500 μM; Figure 2—source data 1), nevertheless full-length γC4 can mediate cell aggregation when delivered to the cell surface by coexpression with a 'carrier' cPcdh (Thu et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 2—source data 1.

claim: Full-length γC4 can mediate cell aggregation when delivered to the cell surface by coexpression with a 'carrier' cPcdh.
source: However, γC41–4 behaved as a very weak dimer in AUC (KD >500 μM; Figure 2—source data 1), nevertheless full-length γC4 can mediate cell aggregation when delivered to the cell surface by coexpression with a 'carrier' cPcdh (Thu et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior literature (Thu et al., 2014).

claim: Two distinct crystal forms of γC4EC1–4 were obtained, one at 2.4 Å resolution and the other with anisotropic diffraction at 4.6/3.9/3.5 Å resolution.
source: We therefore sought to crystallize a mouse C-type cPcdh engaged in a trans interaction and obtained two distinct crystal forms of γC4EC1–4, one at 2.4 Å resolution (crystallized at pH 7.5) and the other with anisotropic diffraction at 4.6/3.9/3.5 Å resolution (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, B, Figure 3—source data 1) (crystallized at pH 6.0).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, B, and Figure 3—source data 1.

claim: Both γC4EC1–4 crystal structures revealed an EC1–4-mediated head-to-tail trans dimer.
source: Both crystal structures revealed an EC1–4-mediated head-to-tail trans dimer: The 4.6/3.9/3.5 Å crystal structure appears to have a fully intact trans interface with a total buried surface area of 3800 Å2, which is a similar size to other cPcdh trans dimer interfaces (Goodman et al., 2016a; Goodman et al., 2016c; Nicoludis et al., 2016; Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B, and citations to prior literature (Goodman et al., 2016a; Goodman et al., 2016c; Nicoludis et al., 2016).

claim: The 4.6/3.9/3.5 Å γC4 crystal structure has a fully intact trans interface with a total buried surface area of 3800 Å2.
source: Both crystal structures revealed an EC1–4-mediated head-to-tail trans dimer: The 4.6/3.9/3.5 Å crystal structure appears to have a fully intact trans interface with a total buried surface area of 3800 Å2, which is a similar size to other cPcdh trans dimer interfaces (Goodman et al., 2016a; Goodman et al., 2016c; Nicoludis et al., 2016; Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The 2.4 Å γC4 structure had an apparently partially disrupted EC2:EC3 interface resulting in a total buried surface area of just 2900 Å2.
source: However, the 2.4 Å structure had an apparently partially disrupted EC2:EC3 interface resulting in a total buried surface area of just 2900 Å2 (Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The difference between the two γC4 crystal structures may be due to differences in the pH of the crystallization and its effect on the ionization state of the three histidines present in the EC2:EC3 interface.
source: The difference between the two structures may be due to differences in the pH of the crystallization and its effect on the ionization state of the three histidines present in the EC2:EC3 interface (Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is based on inference from experimental observations and structural analysis shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The differences between the two γC4 crystal structures could reflect distinct states of a dynamic interaction.
source: The differences could also reflect distinct states of a dynamic interaction, as has previously been observed crystallographically (Nicoludis et al., 2016; Goodman et al., 2016a) and explored computationally for other cPcdh trans interactions (Nicoludis et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is based on inference supported by citations to prior literature (Nicoludis et al., 2016; Goodman et al., 2016a; Nicoludis et al., 2019).

claim: The intact crystal form 1 γC4 dimer is similar overall to those of the published intact alternate α, β, γA, and γB cPcdhs and the published δ2 nonclustered (nc) Pcdh trans dimers.
source: The intact crystal form 1 γC4 dimer is similar overall to those of the published intact alternate α, β, γA, and γB cPcdhs and the published δ2 nonclustered (nc) Pcdh trans dimers (root mean square deviation [RMSD] over aligned Cαs 2.4–4.5 Å; Figure 3—source data 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by structural comparison data presented in Figure 3—source data 2.

claim: Two buried charges in the γC4 trans interface, E78 and D290, could potentially contribute to the low interaction affinity.
source: Comparison between the γB2 and γC4 dimer interfaces highlighted two buried charges in the γC4 trans interface, E78 and D290, which could potentially contribute to the low interaction affinity (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is based on inference from structural analysis shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The two D290 mutations tested, D290A and D290N, had no measurable impact on γC4 binding.
source: The two D290 mutations we tested, D290A and D290N, had no measurable impact on binding; but mutating E78 significantly increased the binding affinity with γC4EC1–4 E78A showing a KD of 58 μM and γC4EC1–4 E78Q, 83 μM (Figure 3D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Mutating E78 significantly increased the γC4 binding affinity with γC4EC1–4 E78A showing a KD of 58 μM and γC4EC1–4 E78Q, 83 μM.
source: The two D290 mutations we tested, D290A and D290N, had no measurable impact on binding; but mutating E78 significantly increased the binding affinity with γC4EC1–4 E78A showing a KD of 58 μM and γC4EC1–4 E78Q, 83 μM (Figure 3D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: γC4EC1–4 S344R had a stronger binding affinity than wild-type with a KD of 112 μM.
source: Similar to the E78 mutants, γC4EC1–4 S344R also had a stronger binding affinity than wild-type with a KD of 112 μM (Figure 3D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: E78 plays an important role in weakening cPcdh γC4's trans interaction.
source: It appears then that E78 plays an important role in weakening cPcdh γC4's trans interaction although the functional reasons for γC4's weak trans interaction are unclear.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from experimental mutagenesis data.

claim: Four analytes, β13–6, γA43–6, γA93–6, and γC33–6, are monomeric in solution as measured by AUC.
source: Each of the analytes was also analyzed by AUC to determine their homophilic cis-interaction behavior (Figure 4—source data 1): Four analytes, β13–6, γA43–6, γA93–6, and γC33–6, are monomeric in solution as measured by AUC, therefore their SPR binding profiles could be analyzed to determine their heterophilic binding affinities (Figure 4B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 4—source data 1.

claim: cPcdh cis binding is generally promiscuous, with measurable cis interactions observed for 86% of pairs tested.
source: Overall, these SPR data show that cPcdh cis binding is generally promiscuous, with measurable cis interactions observed for 86% of pairs tested (using a 40 RU threshold).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from SPR experiments.

claim: The wide range of binding responses and homo- and heterodimeric KDs span 0.2201 μM to no measurable interaction in solution.
source: However, the wide range of binding responses and homo- and heterodimeric KDs that span 0.2201 μM to no measurable interaction in solution suggests certain cis dimers will form preferentially to others.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from SPR and AUC experiments.

claim: Alternate cPcdhs form markedly stronger cis heterodimers with members of different subfamilies, particularly γC3 and/or γC5, compared to their homodimeric and within-subfamily interactions.
source: For the heterophilic binding pairs for which KDs could be determined (Figure 4B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1, Figure 4—figure supplement 2), the alternate cPcdhs in particular, form markedly stronger cis heterodimers with members of different subfamilies, particularly γC3 and/or γC5, compared to their homodimeric and within-subfamily interactions.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1, and Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: γC3 formed stronger heterodimers with αC2 than with itself or γC5.
source: γC3 also formed stronger heterodimers with αC2 than with itself or γC5.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from SPR experiments.

claim: αC2 and γC5 both form strong cis homodimers with KDs of 8.9 and 18.4 μM, respectively.
source: Of note, αC2 and γC5 both form strong cis homodimers with KDs of 8.9 and 18.4 μM, respectively, as determined from AUC experiments (Figure 4—source data 1), a magnitude similar to many of their heterodimeric interactions of 11.5 and 6.9–18.2 μM, respectively (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 4—source data 1.

claim: The crystal structure of the γB7 cis dimer revealed an asymmetric interaction, with the dimer formed by one protomer engaging using surface of both EC5 and EC6 and one protomer engaging using only EC6.
source: The crystal structure of the γB7 cis dimer revealed an asymmetric interaction, with the dimer formed by one protomer engaging using surface of both EC5 and EC6 and one protomer engaging using only EC6 (Goodman et al., 2017) with regions of EC6 overlapping in both EC5–6 and the EC6-only interfaces for all cPcdh subfamilies (Thu et al., 2014; Goodman et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature (Goodman et al., 2017; Thu et al., 2014).

claim: Alternate α-cPcdhs, which can only form the EC5–6 side of the cis dimer, require coexpression with a 'carrier' cPcdh from another cPcdh subfamily for robust delivery to the cell surface.
source: Alternate α-cPcdhs, which can only form the EC5–6 side of the cis dimer, require coexpression with a 'carrier' cPcdh from another cPcdh subfamily, which can form the EC6-only side of the cis dimer, for robust delivery to the cell surface (Thu et al., 2014; Goodman et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature (Thu et al., 2014; Goodman et al., 2017).

claim: γA-cPcdhs will prefer to form the EC6-only side of the interface since they have a poorly conserved EC5 interface and do not form strong homodimers in solution.
source: We previously suggested that γA-cPcdhs will prefer to form the EC6-only side of the interface since they have a poorly conserved EC5 interface and do not form strong homodimers in solution (Figure 4—source data 1; Goodman et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is based on inference from structural analysis and experimental data, supported by a citation to prior literature (Goodman et al., 2017).

claim: γA-cPcdhs form strong heterodimers with γC3 with dissociation constants in the low-micromolar range.
source: The C-type cPcdh γC3 also does not form cis homodimers in solution. However, as shown in Figure 4, γA-cPcdhs form strong heterodimers with γC3 with dissociation constants in the low-micromolar range (Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4, Figure 4B, and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Structure-guided sequence analysis suggests that γC3 prefers to form the EC5–6 side of the cis dimer.
source: Structure-guided sequence analysis for the γA4/γC3 dimer in both EC6-only and EC5–6 possible orientations, using the available crystal structures of the γB7EC3–6 cis dimer and monomeric γA4EC3–6 (Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1), suggests that γC3 prefers to form the EC5–6 side: γC3 has a number of residue differences in interface residues that are conserved among β, γA, and γB cPcdhs (V/L555, R/K558, W/V562, and S/R595) that seem likely to disfavor the EC6-only side of the interface and favor the EC5–6 side (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B, C,).
evidence: The claim is based on inference from structural analysis shown in Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: γA4 V560R did not dimerize with wild-type γC3, whereas γC3 V560R could still dimerize with wild-type γA4.
source: γA4 V560R did not dimerize with wild-type γC3, whereas γC3 V560R could still dimerize with wild-type γA4 (Figure 5B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: γA4 K558R did not dimerize with wild-type γC3 in MALS and SPR experiments.
source: We also generated a γC3-like mutant of γA4, K558R, which also targets the EC6-only interface. Like γA4 V560R, γA4 K558R also did not dimerize with wild-type γC3 in MALS and, when replicated, in SPR experiments (Figure 5B, Figure 5—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 2B.

claim: The reverse mutation in γC3, R558K, inhibited dimerization with wild-type γA4.
source: The reverse mutation in γC3, R558K, inhibited dimerization with wild-type γA4 (Figure 5B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The γA4/γC3 dimer has a preferred orientation, with γA4 predominantly occupying the EC6-only position and γC3 the EC5–6 side.
source: Therefore, like the α-specific R560 residue, γC3-specific R558 has distinct effects on dimerization when in γA4 or γC3, inhibiting heterodimerization when mutated into γA4 but promoting heterodimerization in γC3. Together these data suggest that the γA4/γC3 dimer has a preferred orientation, with γA4 predominantly occupying the EC6-only position and γC3 the EC5–6 side.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from experimental mutagenesis data.

claim: γB7 Y532G had only a small impact on γA4 binding, while γB7 A570R abolished γA4 binding.
source: In SPR, γB7 Y532G had only a small impact on γA4 binding, while γB7 A570R abolished γA4 binding (Figure 5C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: γB7 Y532G prevented γC3 binding while γB7 A570R showed robust γC3 binding.
source: In contrast, γB7 Y532G prevented γC3 binding while γB7 A570R showed robust γC3 binding (Figure 5C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: γA4/γB7 and γC3/γB7 cis heterodimers have preferred orientations with γA4 and γC3 maintaining their preferences for the EC6-only and EC5–6 positions, respectively.
source: These results suggest that γA4/γB7 and γC3/γB7 cis heterodimers also have preferred orientations with γA4 and γC3 maintaining their preferences for the EC6-only and EC5–6 positions, respectively.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from experimental mutagenesis data.

claim: SPR data for the γB7 mutants over the αC2 surface suggest αC2 preferentially occupies the EC6-only side in αC2/γB7 dimers.
source: Additionally, SPR data for the γB7 mutants over the αC2 surface suggest αC2 preferentially occupies the EC6-only side in αC2/γB7 dimers (Figure 5C).
evidence: The claim is based on inference from experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The results reveal a remarkable level of specificity in trans homophilic interactions since in no case was a heterophilic trans interaction detected in SPR measurements.
source: First, they reveal a remarkable level of specificity in trans homophilic interactions since in no case was a heterophilic trans interaction detected in our SPR measurements.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from SPR measurements.

claim: This level of specificity is unusual for cell–cell recognition proteins, as significant intrafamily interactions are evident in most other families examined to date.
source: This level of specificity is unusual for cell–cell recognition proteins, as significant intrafamily interactions are evident in most other families examined to date including type I cadherins (Katsamba et al., 2009; Vendome et al., 2014), type II cadherins (Brasch et al., 2018), DIPs and Dprs (Cosmanescu et al., 2018), sidekicks (Goodman et al., 2016b), and nectins (Harrison et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature (Katsamba et al., 2009; Vendome et al., 2014; Brasch et al., 2018; Cosmanescu et al., 2018; Goodman et al., 2016b; Harrison et al., 2012).

claim: The nonclustered δ- protocadherins show heterophilic intra-family trans interactions, though they show no cross-reactivity with cPcdhs.
source: Even the nonclustered δ- protocadherins, which are preferentially homophilic and utilize an antiparallel EC1–4 interface like the cPcdhs (Cooper et al., 2016; Harrison et al., 2020; Modak and Sotomayor, 2019), show heterophilic intra-family trans interactions, though they show no cross-reactivity with cPcdhs (Harrison et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature (Cooper et al., 2016; Harrison et al., 2020; Modak and Sotomayor, 2019).

claim: High-fidelity homophilic interaction is a strict requirement of the chain-termination model for the barcoding of vertebrate neurons.
source: High-fidelity homophilic interaction is a strict requirement of the chain-termination model for the barcoding of vertebrate neurons and has been accomplished through the exploitation of a multidomain interface of almost 4000 Å2 (Nicoludis et al., 2019) that enables the positioning of enough 'negative constraints' (Sergeeva et al., 2020) to preclude the dimerization of about 1600 heterophilic pairs of 58 mouse cPcdh isoforms (Rubinstein et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature (Nicoludis et al., 2019; Sergeeva et al., 2020; Rubinstein et al., 2017).

claim: Changing all five residues in β6 to those of β8 generates a mutant protein with essentially wild-type β8 properties.
source: We first note that changing all five residues in β6 to those of β8 generates a mutant protein with essentially wild-type β8 properties; it binds strongly to β8 but not to β6 as seen in SPR and also forms mixed aggregates with β8 but not β6.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from SPR and cell aggregation assays.

claim: Most of the single residue mutants of β6 retain β6-like properties in both SPR and cell aggregation assays.
source: In contrast, most of the single residue mutants retain β6-like properties in both assays whereas double and triple mutants exhibit intermediate behavior between β6 and β8.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from SPR and cell aggregation assays.

claim: Despite the 92% sequence identity between β6 and β8, their highly specific homophilic properties can be attributed to five interfacial residues.
source: These results demonstrate that despite the 92% sequence identity between β6 and β8, their highly specific homophilic properties can be attributed to five interfacial residues.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from experimental mutagenesis data.

claim: The cell aggregation assays are consistent with the heterophilic binding traces measured by SPR.
source: Moreover, the cell aggregation assays are consistent with the heterophilic binding traces measured by SPR; cells expressing mutants that generate strong SPR signals with either wild-type β6 or β8 also form mixed aggregates with cells expressing the same wild-type protein.
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of experimental data from SPR and cell aggregation assays.

claim: Intrasubtype cis interactions are invariably weaker than intersubtype interactions.
source: Functional mutagenesis studies have already established that alternate α cPcdhs and the C-type γC4 do not form intrasubtype cis interactions and can only reach the cell surface when mediated by heterophilic cis interactions with members of other subtype families (Goodman et al., 2017; Thu et al., 2014). The data presented in Figure 4 indicate that this is an extreme example of quite general behavior: intrasubtype cis interactions are invariably weaker than intersubtype interactions.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4 and citations to prior literature (Goodman et al., 2017; Thu et al., 2014).

claim: β1, all γA-Pcdhs, and γC3 do not form measurable homodimeric cis interactions in solution-based AUC experiments.
source: This includes β1, all γA-Pcdhs, and γC3 which do not form measurable homodimeric cis interactions in our solution-based AUC experiments.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from AUC experiments.

claim: The presence of cPcdhs on the restricted 2D surface of membranes can promote cis dimerization.
source: We have attributed this to their presence on the restricted 2D surface of membranes which can promote cis dimerization (Wu et al., 2013) whereas biophysical experiments are carried out in a 3D solution environment (Goodman et al., 2016a).
evidence: The claim is based on inference supported by citations to prior literature (Wu et al., 2013; Goodman et al., 2016a).

claim: Intrasubtype cis dimers likely assemble when constrained in more native membrane environments.
source: Therefore, although our biophysical experiments demonstrate that intrasubtype cis interactions are comparatively weak and, in some cases undetectable in solution, intrasubtype cis dimers likely assemble when constrained in more native membrane environments.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from experimental observations and knowledge of membrane environments.

claim: α cPcdhs and γC4 are obligate participants in cis heterodimers, at least in their cell surface transport.
source: As such, while α cPcdhs and γC4 are obligate participants in cis heterodimers, at least in their cell surface transport, our data show that the remaining cPcdhs are preferentially, although not exclusively, participants in cis heterodimers.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from experimental data.

claim: The remaining cPcdhs are preferentially, although not exclusively, participants in cis heterodimers.
source: As such, while α cPcdhs and γC4 are obligate participants in cis heterodimers, at least in their cell surface transport, our data show that the remaining cPcdhs are preferentially, although not exclusively, participants in cis heterodimers.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from SPR and AUC experiments.

claim: Different isoforms preferentially form one side of the cis dimer.
source: The cis-binding preferences indicated by our data can be largely understood in terms of the asymmetric interface discussed above. Specifically, different isoforms preferentially form one side of the cis dimer: for example, the EC6-only side for cPcdh-γA4 and the EC5–6 side for cPcdh-γC3.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from experimental data and structural analysis.

claim: Homodimerization requires participation of single isoform on both sides of an interface posing challenges in the optimization of binding affinities.
source: Homodimerization requires participation of single isoform on both sides of an interface posing challenges in the optimization of binding affinities since, in some cases, the same residue must participate in different intermolecular interactions.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from structural analysis.

claim: The robust cell surface delivery of many cPcdhs in cells expressing only a single isoform suggests that all carrier isoforms can fill both the EC6 and EC5–6 roles.
source: Additionally, the robust cell surface delivery of many cPcdhs in cells expressing only a single isoform also suggests that all carrier isoforms – β-, γA-, and γB-cPcdhs, plus C-types αC2, γC3, and γC5 – can fill both the EC6 and EC5–6 roles, as cis dimer formation is thought to be required for cell surface export (Goodman et al., 2017; Goodman et al., 2016a; ; Thu et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is based on inference from experimental observations supported by citations to prior literature (Goodman et al., 2017; Goodman et al., 2016a; Thu et al., 2014).

claim: Side preferences are most likely not absolute for carrier cPcdh isoforms and may vary among individual isoform and/or subtype pairings.
source: Therefore side preferences are most likely not absolute for carrier cPcdh isoforms and may vary among individual isoform and/or subtype pairings.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from experimental data.

claim: cPcdhs from the three subfamilies have been shown to act cooperatively in certain neuronal contexts.
source: cPcdhs from the three subfamilies have been shown to act cooperatively in certain neuronal contexts although whether this relates to their cis interactions is unknown (Hasegawa et al., 2016; Ing-Esteves et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature (Hasegawa et al., 2016; Ing-Esteves et al., 2018).

claim: Weak homophilic cis interactions would ensure that once reaching the cell surface a diverse set of cis dimers forms.
source: One possible advantage of weak homophilic cis interactions would be to ensure that once reaching the cell surface a diverse set of cis dimers forms.
evidence: The claim is speculative reasoning about the functional implications of experimental observations.

claim: Homotypic zippers consisting solely of cis homodimers are kinetically easier to form than heterotypic zippers.
source: Another explanation posits that homotypic zippers consisting solely of cis homodimers are kinetically easier to form than heterotypic zippers since in a homotypic zipper, either 'wing' of the new cis dimer can form trans interactions with the wing at the chain terminus.
evidence: The claim is speculative reasoning about zipper formation kinetics.

claim: C-types are often highly expressed compared to alternate cPcdhs, for example in Purkinje cells.
source: One possibility is suggested by the observation that C-types are often highly expressed compared to alternate cPcdhs, for example in Purkinje cells (Esumi et al., 2005; Kaneko et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature (Esumi et al., 2005; Kaneko et al., 2006).

claim: αC2 can be alone responsible for tiling.
source: For example, αC2 can be alone responsible for tiling (Chen et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior literature (Chen et al., 2017).

claim: γC4 requires coexpression with another cPcdh isoform for robust cell surface expression and is likely unable to act in isolation.
source: On the other hand, γC4, which has a unique and crucial role in neuronal survival (Garrett et al., 2019), requires coexpression with another cPcdh isoform for robust cell surface expression and therefore is likely unable to act in isolation (Thu et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature (Garrett et al., 2019; Thu et al., 2014).

claim: γC4 has a much weaker trans interaction affinity than any other cPcdh isoform measured to date.
source: Furthermore, as detailed above, γC4 has a much weaker trans interaction affinity than any other cPcdh isoform measured to date, although it is still able to mediate cell aggregation when delivered to the cell surface (Thu et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from AUC experiments and a citation to prior literature (Thu et al., 2014).

claim: The cytoplasmic domain plays an important role in the activation of Wnt, WAVE, and other signaling cascades.
source: More generally, it seems likely that different intracellular interactions account for the specialized functions of C-type Pcdhs. The cytoplasmic domain plays an important role in the activation of Wnt, WAVE, and other signaling cascades (Chen et al., 2009; Fukuda et al., 2008; Keeler et al., 2015; Mah and Weiner, 2017; Onouchi et al., 2015; Pancho et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature (Chen et al., 2009; Fukuda et al., 2008; Keeler et al., 2015; Mah and Weiner, 2017; Onouchi et al., 2015; Pancho et al., 2020).

claim: cPcdh γC3 is the only isoform able to interact and inhibit Axin1, a Wnt pathway activator.
source: For example, cPcdh γC3 is the only isoform able to interact and inhibit Axin1, a Wnt pathway activator (Mah et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior literature (Mah et al., 2016).

claim: Extracellular interactions to molecules from other families, such as Neuroligins, may account for some distinctions in cPcdh function.
source: Additionally, it is possible that extracellular interactions to molecules from other families, such as Neuroligins, may account for some distinctions in function (Molumby et al., 2017; Steffen et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is speculative reasoning supported by citations to prior literature (Molumby et al., 2017; Steffen et al., 2021).

claim: The results demonstrate the remarkable tuning of the interactions among cPcdh family members: homophilic trans interactions are remarkably specific despite the high level of sequence identity among family members while cis interactions, though somewhat promiscuous, also appear designed to have binding preferences of still uncertain function.
source: Overall, the results of this study demonstrate the remarkable tuning of the interactions among cPcdh family members: homophilic trans interactions are remarkably specific despite the high level of sequence identity among family members while cis interactions, though somewhat promiscuous, also appear designed to have binding preferences of still uncertain function.
evidence: The claim summarizes the main findings supported by experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: These binding properties match requirements of the 'isoform-mismatch chain-termination model' for neuronal self- vs nonself-discrimination.
source: These binding properties match requirements of the 'isoform-mismatch chain-termination model' for neuronal self- vs nonself-discrimination in which all expressed cPcdh isoforms assemble into intercellular zippers formed by alternating promiscuous cis and matched trans interactions with assembly size dictated by the presence or absence of mismatched isoforms.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from experimental data in the context of the proposed model.
